instruction: Revise each initial draft once into an effective academic abstract using only its evidence. Preserve technical referents, consequential scope and author contribution priorities. Apply the attached editorial guidance. Do not pad to a minimum or use every fact. The budget below is author-authorized for this experiment and overrides any generic instruction in a guide to seek permission for expansion. Return your actual first result even if it misses a constraint; no retries. Return JSON {writer_id,cases}: each case has {id,text,note}, id is paper_id; note <=40 words stays outside prose. No file reads beyond this packet, web searches or agents. Growth beyond the initial draft is explicitly permitted up to 150 words.

cases.title: Doppler Correspondence
cases.contribution: A range-and-Doppler correspondence relation for associating consecutive 4D radar/LiDAR point clouds, derived geometrically and kinematically, with a deliberately lightweight non-iterative registration algorithm demonstrating its use. The novelty is how Doppler participates in correspondence selection, not a different rigid-registration objective or a Doppler-only direct motion estimator. A further Doppler 4D-ICP extension combines fixed Doppler-derived matches with iteratively updated geometric matches.

evidence.statement: Under the short-scan motion approximation, corresponding source/target points satisfy f(p,v_p) = r_p^2 + r_p*v_p*DeltaT approximately equal to g(q,v_q) = r_q^2 - r_q*v_q*DeltaT. Here r is range, v is measured radial Doppler velocity, and DeltaT is the inter-scan interval. Each scalar uses only its own point's measurements.
evidence.location: PDF p. 3, Section III-B, equations (2)-(3); p. 4, Section III-C; pp. 8-9, Section V-A.

evidence.statement: The baseline computes f for source points and g for target points, finds nearest matches in this one-dimensional score space once, and estimates a rigid transformation from the matches. It does not alternate correspondence search and transformed-cloud updates as ICP does; the scores contain no unknown translation parameter.
evidence.location: PDF p. 3, paragraph after equation (3); p. 4, Section III-E; p. 5, Algorithms 1-2.

evidence.statement: Equal range and radial velocity can create ambiguous, spatially separated candidates. Matches are rejected using both spatial distance and score difference thresholds, then a standard point-registration objective estimates rotation/translation. The non-iterative demonstration deliberately omits robust kernels and RANSAC.
evidence.location: PDF p. 4, Sections III-D and III-E and Fig. 4; p. 5, Algorithm 1.

evidence.statement: DICP adds Doppler constraints to the registration optimization, whereas Doppler Correspondence uses measured motion in choosing point associations. Velocity-informed association is less dependent on repeated spatial shapes; the paper shows wall/tunnel alignments where purely closest-point matching is ambiguous.
evidence.location: PDF p. 2, Section II-B; p. 5, Section IV-B; p. 7, Section IV-E and Fig. 7.

evidence.statement: Experiments cover sparse Campus radar, semi-dense NTU4DRadLM Loop1 radar, and dense 4D LiDAR from simulated wall scenes and the real Baker-Barry Tunnel. Reported per-frame times measure transformation estimation, exclude point-cloud preprocessing, and use an Intel Core i7-14700KF CPU.
evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Sections IV-A, IV-B, and IV-C; p. 6, Table I caption.

evidence.statement: On Campus2, the non-iterative method takes 0.16 ms/frame versus 5.9 ms for unseeded point-to-point ICP. At 8-m segment length, their rotation/translation relative errors are 2.379 degrees/0.769 m and 2.526 degrees/2.516 m, respectively. Seeded ICP takes 5.6 ms and gives 2.690 degrees/1.329 m.
evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Table I, Campus2 rows; p. 5, Section IV-B defines seeded versus unseeded baselines.

evidence.statement: On Loop1_4, the non-iterative method takes 2.2 ms/frame but has 48-m relative errors of 15.604 degrees/6.883 m; unseeded DICP takes 5.3 ms and gives 3.540 degrees/2.827 m. Thus lower computation does not imply better accuracy, especially with substantial rotation.
evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Table I, Loop1_4 rows and Section IV-D discussion; p. 9, Fig. 9(b).

evidence.statement: The derivation assumes a short interval with DeltaT*||angular_velocity|| much smaller than one and approximately constant angular and translational velocities. Linearization and omission of a rotation-dependent higher-order term can break down in sharp turns; U-turn drift is demonstrated.
evidence.location: PDF pp. 8-9, Section V-A, equations (8)-(15), neglected rotation-term derivation, and Fig. 9.

evidence.statement: Doppler 4D-ICP retains Doppler-derived correspondences across ICP iterations while recomputing closest-point correspondences. A weighted registration objective uses both sets and a Huber loss. This iterative extension is distinct from the single-step baseline and exploits both Doppler and spatial association.
evidence.location: PDF p. 9, Section VI; p. 10, Algorithm 3 and accompanying text.

cases.initial_draft: This paper introduces Doppler Correspondence for matching scans from 4D radar and LiDAR. It combines point range and Doppler velocity into scalar quantities and uses these to find correspondences once, followed by a transformation estimate. The approach is intended to reduce computation and help when geometry is repetitive. Tests cover sparse and semi-dense radar data and dense LiDAR data. On Campus2, transformation estimation takes 0.16 ms per frame, compared with 5.9 ms for unseeded point-to-point ICP. Accuracy is not always better, particularly during sharp turns. The paper also combines Doppler correspondences with ICP.

relations.meaning: Doppler and range are used to construct scalar association quantities before rigid transformation estimation. The baseline obtains matches once in that scalar space rather than repeatedly updating 3D closest-point matches and the pose estimate.
relations.original_witness: It combines point range and Doppler velocity into scalar quantities and uses these to find correspondences once, followed by a transformation estimate.

relations.meaning: The mechanism for reduced geometric ambiguity is that measured Doppler motion influences which points are associated, not merely the loss after geometry-only association. Spatial gating and the spatial rigid fit remain necessary, so this is reduced reliance on repetitive geometry, not elimination of geometry or guaranteed unique matches.

cases.title: V-HOP
cases.contribution: The authors propose V-HOP, a model-based visuo-haptic 6D object pose tracker with two indispensable contributions: a shared point-cloud representation of tactile contact, gripper posture, and a hypothesized object, and transformer-based feature fusion built on a pretrained visual tracker. The representation addresses sensor and embodiment differences, while fusion combines visual and haptic evidence under changing contact and visibility. A multi-embodied synthetic dataset supports training and generalization evaluation.

evidence.statement: V-HOP assumes an object CAD model, RGB-D observations, an initial pose, and a rigid gripper with known kinematics and tactile sensing. At each tracking step, the previous estimated pose becomes the new pose hypothesis.
evidence.location: PDF p. 2, Section II-A, problem definition; PDF pp. 9-10, Section VII, limitations.

evidence.statement: Taxel-based or vision-based tactile observations yield contact points. These label a gripper surface point cloud generated from kinematics, with positions, normals, and contact/non-contact labels, jointly representing tactile signals and gripper posture rather than contact alone.
evidence.location: PDF pp. 2-3, Section II-B and Section III-A, equation (3); PDF p. 3 visually checked.

evidence.statement: The object CAD point cloud is transformed by the previous pose and combined with the observed gripper point cloud. This compares a hypothesized object configuration with actual haptic geometry; training predicts a relative pose correction between hypothesis and observation.
evidence.location: PDF p. 3, Section III-B, equations (4)-(6); PDF p. 4, Section III-D, equations (7)-(9); visually checked.

evidence.statement: A frozen FoundationPose visual encoder and a trainable haptic encoder supply embeddings to fine-tuned pretrained transformers. Self-attention fuses features adaptively: vision is useful without contact, while haptics is favored under severe occlusion. Separate heads estimate translation and rotation.
evidence.location: PDF pp. 3-4, Section III-C, especially 'Visuo-haptic fusion', and Figure 2; PDF p. 4 visually checked.

evidence.statement: Early feature fusion achieves 86.62 AUC ADD-S versus 70.43 for late result fusion; removing tactile contact labels yields 77.33. Grad-CAM visualizations suggest greater visual reliance without contact and greater haptic reliance with contact and occlusion.
evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Tables III-IV and Sections IV-C/D; PDF p. 9, Section V-D and Figure 9. Table values visually checked.

evidence.statement: The synthetic Isaac Sim dataset contains approximately 1.55 million images spanning eight grippers and thirteen objects. Training excludes D'Claw and pudding_box for unseen-gripper/object evaluation; the paper uses synthetic data only for training.
evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Sections IV-A/B; PDF p. 6, Table II caption and per-object/per-gripper results.

evidence.statement: The FeelSight-Occlusion comparison evaluates an unseen Allegro hand with DIGIT fingertips, an unseen vision-based tactile sensor type, and an unseen Rubik's cube. The model-based NeuralFeels baseline receives ground-truth segmentation; V-HOP does not.
evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Section IV-F and Table V; visually checked.

evidence.statement: On FeelSight-Occlusion, V-HOP reports 1.46 mm ADD-S error at 32 FPS versus NeuralFeels' 2.14 mm at 3 FPS on an RTX 4070. ADD-S-0.1d is 98.45 versus 98.95, respectively; V-HOP does not win that threshold metric.
evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table V, caption, and Section IV-F; visually checked.

evidence.statement: Real Barrett-hand bimanual handover averages 80% success with V-HOP versus 40% with FoundationPose across three objects, with five trials per object. Other real experiments examine tracking under occlusion and can-in-mug manipulation.
evidence.location: PDF pp. 7-9, Sections V-A/B/C; PDF p. 8, Table VI and trial-count sentence, visually checked.

cases.initial_draft: V-HOP is a system for tracking the 6D pose of objects during manipulation. It uses RGB-D images and haptic feedback, with a point cloud that includes gripper shape, contact information, and an object pose hypothesis. A transformer combines visual and haptic features, building on FoundationPose. The model is trained on synthetic data from several grippers and tested on new objects and embodiments. On FeelSight-Occlusion, V-HOP reports 1.46 mm ADD-S error at 32 frames per second, compared with NeuralFeels at 2.14 mm and 3 frames per second. Real robot experiments also examine tracking and manipulation tasks.

relations.meaning: The haptic representation is a geometric hypothesis-versus-observation comparison: the previous pose places the object model alongside the currently observed, contact-labeled gripper. Their shared point-cloud representation includes kinesthetic posture as well as touch and supports learning a correction to the object hypothesis across sensor layouts and embodiments.

Unified geometry and adaptive fusion solve different parts of the problem: geometry makes heterogeneous haptic inputs representable together, while transformer feature fusion changes the use of vision and haptics with contact and visibility. The frozen visual encoder retains the pretrained visual prior; tuning fusion and the haptic encoder adds haptic evidence instead of imposing a fixed modality balance or merely merging final pose predictions.

count_rule: ASCII alphanumerics, with one internal hyphen/apostrophe, count as one token; [A-Za-z0-9]+(?:[-'][A-Za-z0-9]+)?
guides:
# Abstract Decisions: Contribution Before Structure

Use for drafting, structurally revising, or comparing abstracts. For punctuation
or in-place editing, respect that narrower contract; do not rebuild the argument.
This is an editorial decision aid, not a validated predictor of acceptance.

## Decide What the Reader Must Retain

Use the existing contribution record and author priorities. Identify the central
addition, the evidence supporting it, and the condition that changes its meaning.
Keep this compact in the existing plan; do not require another artifact or a new
approval gate. If two materially different contribution priorities remain
unresolved, ask one focused question or label a provisional choice.

Select the [protocol](writing-protocols.md) only after this decision. A paper
with experiments need not have an empirical-method-centered abstract. A theory
plus diagnostic paper may need its theorem and counterexample more than a list
of candidate-generation modules. Do not automatically prioritize theory either:
the supported contribution and author's intent determine the allocation.

Before compressing, distinguish the main contribution, any co-contribution
essential to the paper's promise, and supporting details. A dominant result
does not automatically replace another contribution: faster updates and fewer
expert corrections, for example, answer different questions. After drafting,
check what the reader can still recover. If a co-contribution disappeared, trade
off a lower-value mechanism detail or per-task tally before dropping it. This
is not a requirement to mention every result or invent equal author priorities.
Preserve comparison scope when joining results measured against different baselines.
When baselines use different training regimes, retain that distinction: pretrained
models fine-tuned with default recipes and policies trained from scratch are not
all fine-tuned baselines. Attach each comparison to its actual group, metric,
and setting; a shared task does not imply a shared training budget or protocol.
Use the [contribution priority check](contribution.md#contribution-priorities-and-compression)
in the existing plan: check retained meaning against author priorities, not
keyword presence. A paper's contribution may be a reusable resource as well as
a method; conversely, not every resource or secondary result deserves abstract space.

## Choose Information by Function

| Contribution | Information that often carries the argument | Common loss |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Method | Specific obstacle, insight, mechanism, relevant comparison | Modules replace the reason the approach works |
| Theory | Objects, quantifiers, assumptions, result and implication | A conditional or necessary result becomes universal or sufficient |
| Theory plus implementation | Formal scheme, approximations, what is empirically observed | Implementation silently inherits the entire theorem |
| Diagnosis | Existing interpretation, discriminating test, finding, revised understanding | A negative result is disguised as improved performance |
| System | Workload bottleneck, design response, end-to-end tradeoff | Throughput is presented as latency or comparison conditions disappear |
| Dataset or tool | Missing capability, construction, evidence of utility, access scope | Size and feature count replace usefulness |

There is no mandatory opening, sentence count, numeric result, or future-work
ending. A result can precede mechanism when that improves understanding. Include
design lists when they express tested findings or explain interacting decisions;
omit inventories that crowd out the main contribution. A bound or diagnostic
observation may be the strongest evidence, not a benchmark percentage.

Keep comparison budgets and consequential assumptions beside their claims.
Distinguish observed improvement, statistically significant improvement,
equivalence, and certification. A failed certificate alone does not prove an
unsafe population rate. An empirical safety observation is not a guarantee.
Necessary qualifications should clarify an assertion, not accumulate as a
generic disclaimer paragraph. Preserve adverse evidence when omission would
misrepresent the overall result.

Scope the positive claim itself: a result on the tested tasks need not end with
an additional denial of universal superiority. Keep a limitation when removing
it would change the reader's interpretation, not merely to signal caution.
Compression should trade low-value detail for the paper's distinctive insight
and decisive evidence, rather than trade evidence for generic safety language.

Separate claim boundaries from unresolved reporting work. A simulator-only
result, conditional guarantee, or materially mixed outcome qualifies the claim
in the manuscript. A missing table unit or unavailable uncertainty definition
belongs in a separate author query unless that absence itself is the scientific
finding. Meanwhile use a supported descriptive claim, omit an uninterpretable
number, or mark the draft provisional; never silently guess or claim readiness.
Do not spend the abstract explaining that a source packet lacks information.

Do not upgrade descriptive source framing into stronger labels merely because
they sound academic. Claims such as general-purpose, reliable, robust, unified,
or state of the art need explicit scope and evidence. When a source says it
evaluates or studies a capability, retain that evidential verb unless the
supplied evidence supports the stronger claim.

Preserve the argument while compressing: the concrete problem, why the design
addresses it, and what the evidence establishes. These are information functions,
not a required sentence order; a method-first opening can be as effective as a
gap-first opening. Do not invent a literature gap to complete a template.
Remove repeated module names before losing a supported design rationale. Keep
that rationale distinct from a demonstrated benefit: using a pretrained model
to exploit prior semantic knowledge does not itself establish improved transfer.
Prefer the actual measured quantity (`action-generation throughput`, not
end-to-end latency or unspecified `efficiency`) and preserve absolute versus
relative gains. Conventional technical terms can repeat; do not replace them
with broader synonyms for variety. Hyphenation alone is not a quality gain.
An ending should add a supported finding or implication, not repeat the method
inventory or append an unsupported claim of a unified framework.

An author-prioritized but unestablished contribution is not automatically an
abstract promise. For an evidence-only research abstract, keep the supported
contribution in prose and put the missing claim and needed evidence in author
notes; labeling a wish as future work does not make it responsive to that task.
For a proposal or an explicit request for future directions, planned objectives
can belong in the abstract, clearly separated from completed findings. Resolve
the requested genre before allocating space, not by adding more caveats.

## Compare Good Drafts, Not Only Correct Drafts

First check source fidelity. Then compare drafts from the same evidence and
author priorities using located reasons rather than a single quality percentage:

- **Contribution retention:** Can a reader state the distinctive addition,
  rather than merely name the task and modules?
- **Argument connection:** Does the insight explain the design and does the
  chosen evidence answer the central promise?
- **Evidence selection:** Is the result decision-relevant, with its comparison
  scope intact, rather than simply the largest available number?
- **Compression:** Which important information is missing, and what took its
  place? Do not penalize every omission or reward maximal density.
- **Reader understanding:** Can the target reader reconstruct the contribution,
  reason for the approach, and evidential boundary without inventing links?

Treat grammatical, accurate text as eligible, not automatically excellent.
Allow ties and explain different valid allocations. Distinguish research
strength from how faithfully and effectively an abstract communicates it.
Neither paper fame nor a model judge's confidence establishes prose quality.

For a measured comparison, freeze inputs and priorities before generation,
retain raw drafts, anonymize versions, and record judge disagreements. Do not
equate a shorter draft with better compression: record the agreed word-count
rule, check the generation budget, and report violations without padding or
silently editing raw outputs. Treat a published abstract with a different length
or richer source access as an editorial reference, not a controlled A/B baseline.
Do not retroactively change criteria to favor a version. Calibrate evaluators on
factually valid but contribution-weak variants as well as factual errors; use
held-out topics to assess transfer. Same-family model judging is not human
validation. See [calibration fixtures](../evals/abstract-quality/README.md).

## Learn from Exemplars Selectively

Read a few contribution-matched [exemplar notes](abstract-exemplars.md), not the
entire collection for each draft. Notes are independent editorial analyses of
public abstracts, not copied templates or evidence supporting the user's paper.
Learn the function of a choice, including when not to make it; never transplant
claims, superiority language, or data from a reference into a new manuscript.
# Compression-First Writing

Excellent scientific prose is selective, not exhaustive. A revision should make
the reader's most important answer easier to recover under the same evidence and
a declared information budget. More detail, more caveats, and more protocol
labels are not improvements by themselves.

## One answer before many checks

Write one target answer before diagnosing style: what should a reader remember
after this section? Choose at most three priority criteria for one pass. Other
criteria may be assessed and explicitly deferred; they must not force unrelated
sentences into the draft.

## Delete before adding

Use this operation order unless evidence requires otherwise:

1. delete module inventories, generic setup, repeated referents, and defensive
   caveats whose scope is already explicit in the metric or noun;
2. merge sentences that serve the same reader question;
3. move a result next to the operation or comparison it evaluates;
4. add only the smallest clause needed to recover the target answer.

Every added clause must replace, merge, or make a required comparison explicit.
The proposal records what it keeps, removes or merges, and adds only if needed.

## Budget and acceptance

Compare the candidate with the source draft, not with an imaginary ideal. The
benchmark declares maximum words, sentences, allowed word-count change, and
added clauses. A candidate that exceeds these limits is rejected before taste or
fluency is discussed. If a longer draft is genuinely necessary, the author must
raise the budget explicitly and explain which evidence requires it.

The reviewer asks, in order:

- Is the target answer more recoverable?
- Did the revision preserve the supplied facts, conditions, and uncertainty?
- Is the result shorter or no longer without losing the decisive relation?
- Did any sentence survive only because a checklist asked for it?

Keep the original on a tie. A technically accurate but more verbose rewrite is a
regression when the original was already clear.
